questions.question: Why should a motorcycle work area be kept clean and dry?
options: To reduce slip, trip, and fire hazards
To make tools harder to find
questions.explanation:
A clean floor reduces slips caused by oil, coolant, or water.
A tidy work area also prevents trips over tools and parts.
Good housekeeping is a basic shop safety practice.

questions.category: A2 — Use personal protective equipment (PPE) and safety equipment
questions.question: Why should safety glasses be worn when grinding or cutting?
options: To protect the eyes from sparks and debris
questions.explanation:
Grinding and cutting can send metal fragments into the air.
Safety glasses protect the eyes from serious injuries.
They are standard PPE for many shop tasks.

questions.question: Why should the correct threadlocker be used on fasteners when specified?
options: To help prevent fasteners from loosening
questions.explanation:
Vibration can loosen fasteners on motorcycles during operation.
Threadlocker helps hold specified bolts and screws in place.
It must be used only where required by service information.

questions.category: B2 — Perform periodic maintenance of lubrication systems
questions.question: Why should engine oil level be checked regularly?
options: Low oil can lead to engine damage
questions.explanation:
Engine oil lubricates, cools, and protects moving parts.
If the level gets too low, internal wear increases quickly.
Regular checks help prevent major engine damage.

questions.category: B3 — Perform periodic maintenance of cooling systems
questions.question: Why should coolant level be checked in a liquid-cooled motorcycle?
questions.explanation:
Coolant removes heat from the engine and radiator system.
If the level is too low, the engine may overheat.
Regular inspection helps prevent cooling system failure.
